proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (rescaled area formula), with the Jacobian kept abstract. In the parent, J = areaJacobianAt F and the area hypothesis is SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn (step 0(f)).
Notation:
- A := F(B), y := F(b), η := η_{y,r}, so η(z) = r^{-1}(z − y);
- λ := volume on ℝ^n and H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^P;
- ν := the measure λ⌞B with density x ↦ ofReal(J(x)) = ((J x).toNNReal : [0,∞]);
- G(a) := 1_B(a)·J(a)·f(r^{-1}(F(a) − y)) for a ∈ ℝ^n.
1. Scaling. Apply the sibling pit_setIntegral_blowUpMap_image with M := A and x := y: ∫_{η(A)} f dH^n = r^{-n} ∫_A f(η(z)) dH^n(z).
2. The area hypothesis as a measure identity: H^n⌞A = F_#ν. F is continuous, hence Borel. Let T ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and apply the hypothesis to g := 1_T.
- Left side: ∫⁻_A 1_T dH^n = (H^n⌞A)(T) (lintegral_indicator_one).
- Right side: ofReal(J(x))·1_T(F(x)) = 1_{F^{-1}(T)}(x)·ofReal(J(x)) for every x. So the right side is ∫⁻_{F^{-1}(T)} ofReal(J) d(λ⌞B) (lintegral_indicator; F^{-1}(T) is Borel). This equals ν(F^{-1}(T)) (withDensity_apply), which equals (F_#ν)(T) (Measure.map_apply).
- Measures agreeing on all Borel sets are equal (Measure.ext).
3. Transfer of the Bochner integral. The function h := f∘η is continuous (η is affine), hence strongly measurable.
- By step 2 and integral_map (F is measurable), ∫_A h dH^n = ∫ h d(F_#ν) = ∫ h(F(x)) dν(x).
- By integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul with the Borel density x ↦ (J x).toNNReal, this is ∫_B (J x).toNNReal · h(F(x)) dλ(x) = ∫_B J(x)·h(F(x)) dλ(x), since ((J x).toNNReal : ℝ) = J(x) when J ≥ 0.
- As B is Borel, integral_indicator gives ∫_B J(x)·h(F(x)) dλ(x) = ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(x)·J(x)·h(F(x)) dλ(x) = ∫ G dλ. Here h(F(x)) = f(r^{-1}(F(x) − y)) by the definition of blowUpMap.
- These identities hold for arbitrary integrands, so no integrability is needed.
4. Substitution a = b + rc. λ is an additive Haar measure on ℝ^n and finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
- Measure.integral_comp_smul applied to x ↦ G(b + x) gives ∫ G(b + rc) dλ(c) = |(r^n)^{-1}| ∫ G(b + x) dλ(x).
- Translation invariance (integral_add_left_eq_self) gives ∫ G(b + x) dλ(x) = ∫ G dλ. Both identities hold for every function.
- Since r > 0, ∫ G(b + rc) dλ(c) = r^{-n} ∫ G dλ.
5. Combining steps 1, 3 and 4: ∫_{η(A)} f dH^n = r^{-n} ∫_A f∘η dH^n = r^{-n} ∫ G dλ = ∫ G(b + rc) dλ(c).
Finally G(b + rc) = 1_B(b + rc)·J(b + rc)·f(r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b))) = B.indicator J (b + r • c) · f (r⁻¹ • (F (b + r • c) − F b)), the stated integrand.
Remark: compared with step 4 of the parent proof, the measure identity of step 2 makes the integrability estimates of 4(i) and 4(iii) unnecessary. In particular no co-Lipschitz or finiteness hypothesis is used.

The area hypothesis with indicator weights gives H^n⌞F(B) = F_#((λ⌞B) with density ofReal∘J).
integral_map, integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul and integral_indicator give ∫_{F(B)} f∘η dH^n = ∫ 1_B·J·(f∘η∘F) dλ.
